text:
Maria G: Heads-up — running a TP throughput sweep on 8xA100 (v5 runtime) and hit a reproducible latency bump for all-reduce at ~3–9KB per-rank. baseline throughput drops ~3x in that band. :thinking:
Jon K: Fwiw that's where our coalescing heuristics sometimes produce uneven stripe boundaries. Can you paste the perf log? :eyes:
Maria G: paste from the repro run (shortened):
```
[run] tp_test --model resnet-tiny --tp 8 --microbs 16 --steps 200
allreduce mean: 42.1 ms (3–9KB) vs 6.2 ms (<3KB) and 8.0 ms (>9KB)
nccl version: 2.12.10
RUNTIME_KERNEL: default-kernel-v2
KV cache enabled: true
Batching: adaptive (max_pad=256)
```
Samir P: That shape is suspicious — small-ish messages but enough fragments to trigger non-contiguous chunking + NCCL rendezvous handshake overhead. Could be stripe packing + unexpected kernel fallback.
Kevin L: Do we see a kernel selector flip at that size? I remember a threshold in kernel-selector: if msg_bytes > 4096 it picks kernel-B which performs worse for narrow stripes.
Maria G: I dumped the selector decisions around the spike:
```
msg_bytes=3072 -> kernel-A (fast)
msg_bytes=4096 -> kernel-B (slow)
msg_bytes=6144 -> kernel-B (slow)
```
So yes, borderline region flips to kernel-B and NCCL enters an extra handshake path that costs ~30ms.
perf-bot: flamegraph uploaded: http://perf.internal/fg/2890012345 (shows NCCL handshake + kernel-B wait) :chart_with_upwards_trend:
Jon K: Two immediate hypotheses: (1) our kernel selector threshold is too coarse for TP stripe sizes and doesn't account for NCCL algorithm selection; (2) KV-cache/coalesce policy produces a fragmentation pattern that lands many ops in the kernel-B region.
Samir P: Quick repro idea: force kernel-A for all sizes and see if latency stabilizes. We can also try forcing NCCL to use tree algorithm for these msg sizes to compare.
Kevin L: Could try NCCL_ALGO=tree and NCCL_PROTO=LL128 override in the repro job. Also try padding-to-8KB vs padding-to-16KB to see where cost amortizes.
Maria G: I ran a quick patch to pad to 8KB and force kernel-A:
```
export NCCL_ALGO=ring
# patch: selector.patch (one-line fallback)
# if (msg_bytes in borderline) choose kernel-A
```
Result: allreduce ~7.1 ms across the board, throughput back to normal. Padding wins.
Jon K: Nice. Padding is an ok mitigation for now but we should fix root cause: selector + NCCL algo interplay. We should also avoid blind padding for cost reasons.
Samir P: Longer-term fix: make kernel selector aware of communicator topology and NCCL algo choice. If NCCL chooses a handshake-heavy path for small stripes, bias selector toward kernels that favor minimal handshakes. Also teach coalescer to prefer even stripe boundaries across TP peers.
Kevin L: We should also add a unit perf test in CI that exercises the 2–10KB per-rank range with 8xTP and asserts p99 < 12ms.
Maria G: I'll open an issue with repro script + logs and assign. Quick notes I'll add to the ticket: env, exact cmd, perf-bot link, raw flamegraph, kernel-selector dump, and a minimal patch that pads to 8KB as a stopgap.
Jon K: If someone has bandwidth, try NCCL env toggles: NCCL_ALGO=tree, NCCL_PROTO=SIMPLE, and NCCL_MIN_NRINGS=1. Those change handshake behavior.
Samir P: One extra datapoint — we saw similar behavior on 4xH100 but with smaller bump (2x) — suggests hardware-specific kernel latency matters but algorithm handshake is dominant.
Kevin L: Also check whether KV cache eviction causes intermittent bursts of backend traffic that coincidentally align with stripe boundaries. If cache flush happens at a bad boundary, it could produce uneven msg sizes.
Maria G: Good call. I'll instrument KV flush timings in next run. For now, creating the issue: https://redwood.internal/issue/RT-4562 and attaching the logs. Assigning to Samir + Jon to propose a selector/coalesce fix.
Samir P: I'll prototype a selector rule that considers (msg_bytes, tp_peers, nccl_algo_hint) and logs decisions to perf. Expect a PR next week. :thumbsup:
Jon K: Thanks — let's sync in the weekly runtime triage and mark this P1 perf regression for TP workloads.
Kevin L: cheers, everyone.
Maria G: Thanks all — saved the padded run as fallback in cluster configs for the short term. :white_check_mark:
